rv.q: Bedlam's artistic director Eric Tucker applies the inventive staging techniques on which the company has built its reputation to a good old-fashioned story set to excellent songs. What more could you want?
Each of his songs are perfectly set into this story, arranged with excellent harmonies when called for, and gives each character who sings them a great moment to shine.
Music City provides plenty of drama and the right songs to go with it.
The vocals on this cast is astonishing.

Fortune would appear to be smiling on brothers T.J. and Drew, who grew up in foster homes but, as the show opens, earn the attention of a big record company executive on the strength of T.J.’s catchy, upbeat songs. (Drew, as he admits, just comes up with the titles.).
Music City makes a tempting cocktail of an irresistible cast, barn-burning country songs, and stellar orchestration.
Music City is a loud, lived-in jukebox musical that finally finds its heart the moment Lauren "LOLO" Pritchard picks up a guitar.

cn.t: Critics praise this immersive Nashville-set jukebox musical for its inventive staging and strong songs, with Bedlam transforming the venue into a dive bar. The show earns solid marks for its engaging performances and country music atmosphere.

vr.q: The plot loses some steam in Act 2, but you're never far from a good song at any given moment.
